title: What is known about 1RB0LC_1LC0RE_1LD1LC_1LA1RD_1RF1RB_---0RB
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LC_1LC0RE_1LD1LC_1LA1RD_1RF1RB_---0RB.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state machine halts from blank tape. Seen from the left end, its tape is a few long blocks of 1s separated by single 0s; the block lengths keep being cut into halves and thirds (2,666 and 1,332; 1,318, 1,975 and 655; 332, 1,489, 1,652 and 494). Seen from the right end, the left part of the tape is an alternating stretch 1 0 1 0 … and the rest a solid block.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves no halt in the first 107 steps; the C simulator shows none in 109. How the block lengths are cut is not yet understood.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 4,003 cells have been visited and 2,945 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Tape shape
claims.text: At the last left-end extensions before 109 steps the tape is two to four blocks of 1s split by single 0s, e.g. 0 1^2666 0 1^1332 at step 999,181,386, 0 1^1318 0 1^1975 0 1^655 at step 959,766,361, 0 1^332 0 1^1489 0 1^1652 0 1^494 at step 974,655,988. At the right-end side switches the left part is alternating, with holes, and the rest a solid block or more alternating cells: (10)^1333 1^1336 0 at step 999,185,396, (10)^666 0 (10)^993 1^664 0 at step 981,117,700, (10)^1328 0 (10)^661 at step 978,904,600.

claims.title: Growth shape: power/power
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.336). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.334).

claims.title: Growth like t<sup>1/3</sup>
claims.text: After step 5·10<sup>8</sup>: 291 side switches, 1,720,135 steps apart on average (≈ 0.107·w<sup>2</sup>, w = 4002), about 2.9 cells of width per switch; fitted width exponent 0.335 after step 10<sup>7</sup>.

claims.title: How it could halt
claims.text: The halting transition is F reading 0. F is entered only from E reading 0, moving right. So a halt is exactly E>0 0: E on a 0 with a 0 to its right. E is entered only from B reading 1, which writes 0, so equivalently B>1 0 0.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The shapes above hold at every extension printed; what rule cuts the blocks, and why B never meets a 1 followed by two 0s, are open.

check: gcc -O2 -o tmrun tools/c/tmrun.c && ./tmrun 1RB0LC_1LC0RE_1LD1LC_1LA1RD_1RF1RB_---0RB 1000000000 records 100000 > rec.txt && python3 holdouts/1RB0LC_1LC0RE_1LD1LC_1LA1RD_1RF1RB_---0RB/py/shape.py rec.txt a=10 && python3 holdouts/1RB0LC_1LC0RE_1LD1LC_1LA1RD_1RF1RB_---0RB/py/switches.py rec.txt a=10

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. The tape is a few long blocks of 1s with single 0s between them, and on each trip the block lengths are cut in halves or thirds and rejoined. Each trip crosses the whole tape and costs about the width squared, for a few cells of growth: the width grows like the cube root of the time.

facts.text: Width of the tape at its last extension before step 10<sup>9</sup>.
Side switches in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps.

sections.heading: Blocks of 1s, cut and rejoined
html: The tape at a few left-end extensions near the end of the first 109 steps (head at the far left):

The first block keeps being halved (1,318, 661, 332) and then the blocks merge back into a 2:1 pair (2,651 and 1,323). At the right end the left part of the tape reads as an alternating stretch: (10)^1333 1^1336 0 at step 999,185,396, about a third of the width alternating, then a solid block.

sections.heading: Why the width grows like t<sup>1/3</sup>
html: The head goes back and forth across the whole tape. After step 5·108 there are 291 side switches (extensions of the tape on the other side from the last one), on average 1,720,135 steps apart, which is about 0.107·w2 for the final width w = 4002; each adds about 2.9 cells to the width. A constant gain per w2 steps gives w3 ~ t. The fitted exponent of the width after step 107 is 0.335.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.336). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.334).
After 109 steps the tape spans 4,003 cells (2,433 left of the start, 813 right), with a density of 1s of 0.736.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

family: blocks of 1s split in halves and thirds
summary: At the left end the tape is two to four blocks of 1s separated by single 0s, with lengths in ratios near 2:1 or halved again; at the right end it is an alternating stretch followed by a solid block. Width ~ t^(1/3).
